frozen_before: any post-fill bar or 04:30 quote was fetched for this replay; YYAI and NCPL (Oct 14) are the only fills examined so far, and they motivated the test
purpose: Juan, Oct 15: 'YYAI good entry, late exit.' Does a resting sell limit placed right after each AH buy fill beat the live 04:30 ET sell-all exit?
fills: every filled after-hours buy order on the Alpaca paper account PA37U2Y192A7 from 2026-06-25 to 2026-10-15 (buy filled_at between 16:00 and 20:00 ET), one row per order, at its filled_avg_price
baseline: sell at the bid of the latest SIP quote in 04:00-04:30 ET on the next trading day (the live rule since Oct 14); rows without a valid quote use the first 1-minute SIP bar open at or after 04:00 ET and are counted
fill_rule: the limit fills at the limit price if any 1-minute SIP bar starting after the fill minute and before 20:00 ET on D, or from 04:00 to 04:29 ET on D+1, has a high strictly above the limit; otherwise the row takes the baseline exit
unit: return per trade = exit / fill - 1; equal weight; the comparison is the paired difference variant minus baseline
statistics: mean paired difference with a bootstrap over fill dates (4000 draws, seed 13), two-sided interval with tail 0.025/3 (Bonferroni over 3 variants); also report fill rate, mean return per variant, and the fills since Oct 12 listed individually
pass: a variant passes if the mean paired difference > 0 AND its interval lower bound > 0 AND both chronological halves have a positive mean difference
decision_if_pass: report the passing variant to Juan in the daily email with the evidence; it changes live exits, so it is wired only if he does not object (Juan's routing of this item, FEEDBACK_LOG 2026-10-16)
decision_if_fail: report that a resting take-profit does not beat the 04:30 exit on paper fills; no change
limits: bar highs are trade prints, so a fill strictly above the limit is assumed to have filled the resting order; quoted size and queue position are ignored; the 20:00-04:00 overnight session is excluded; fills are real paper fills from strategies that changed over time; n is about 100.
